title: Mediawan’s Pierre-Antoine Capton on Buying Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine and Doubling Down on Hollywood Amid Consolidation (EXCLUSIVE)
description: After buying Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment in 2022 and Peter Chernin’s North Road earlier this year, Mediawan has enlisted another major Hollywo
body:
After buying Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment in 2022 and Peter Chernin’s North Road earlier this year, Mediawan has enlisted another major Hollywood player, Reese Witherspoon‘s Hello Sunshine.

	As with its previous acquisitions which were financed partly through stock, Mediawan is bringing Witherspoon into its shareholder base, joining a stellar roster of talent and producers who have invested in the Paris-based group, including Pitt, Chernin and Plan B partners Dede Gardner and Jeremy Kleiner, as well as See-Saw’s Iain Canning and Emilie Sherman. The company also launched LuckyChap International, the London-based arm of Margot Robbie’s company, last November.
	

	“For our tenth anniversary today, we’re working with Brad Pitt, Margot Robbie, and Reese Witherspoon — all three of whom are extremely creative and recognized as such — it defines the company’s DNA in terms of its independence, its commitment to talent, and its creativity,” said Mediawan co-founder and chairman Pierre-Antoine Capton in an exclusive interview with Variety less than a day after unveiling the deal.


	Mediawan also managed to pick up Hello Sunshine at a fraction of the $900 million valuation the company had when Blackstone-backed Candle Media acquired a majority stake in 2021.

	Variety understands that Mediawan paid the lower end of the tens of millions of dollars, although Capton declined to disclose the exact figure or financial terms. 

	“I can’t confirm. The bottom line is that we acquired 100% of Hello Sunshine along with Reese and Mediawan, from Candle Media, and the money we’re investing is going toward development and content creation. It’s truly being invested in the company,” said Capton, who credited Chernin and Jesse Jacobs, former shareholders in Hello Sunshine, for bringing the opportunity to Mediawan. 
	

	The momentum has shifted in favor of European companies, as traditional Hollywood power players are under pressure to cut costs, streaming platforms are becoming pickier, and U.S. indie producers are eager to work in Europe, where they can produce at lower costs and own IP. While Mediawan has made a name for itself in Hollywood in the last five years, another European giant with French roots, Banijay, which just merged with British powerhouse All3Media, is also looking to invest in the U.S. scripted market where it hasn’t yet broken through. 

	The acquisition of Hello Sunshine by Mediawan also illustrates how much the business has changed since the streaming boom that fueled Hello Sunshine’s previous valuation. Candle Media, founded by former Disney executives Kevin Mayer and Tom Staggs, had bet heavily on Witherspoon’s star power, social media presence and Reese’s Book Club, but that model became more difficult to monetize in recent years.

	On whether Hello Sunshine would fare better under Mediawan than it did under Candle, Capton pointed to the prestigious track record of Witherspoon’s company, notably “Big Little Lies,” “The Morning Show” and the Apple TV series “Lucky,” adapted from a Reese’s Book Club selection.

	“They’ve really excelled creatively. That said, unfortunately, from time to time, there are investment deals with companies that may be perceived as financial strategies. That’s not the case for us,” said Capton, who worked on the deal alongside Mediawan CEO Elisabeth D’Arvieu and Guillaume Izabel, head of strategy and M&A. “With Reese, we’re really looking for creativity, independence, and vision. That’s what interests us, so we don’t put financial pressure on it. It’s truly an editorial, artistic, and creative addition that we’re seeking.”

	Capton also said Mediawan intends to bring Reese’s Book Club internationally, including through potential productions in France and elsewhere in Europe.

	“For all Mediawan producers — whether they’re Italian, German, British, or Australian — access to all the IP that Reese can leverage through her Book Club is something very rare,” Capton said. “Yesterday, when we announced Reese and Hello Sunshine’s arrival at Mediawan, all our producers called us asking: How can we work with them? How can we access the IP? How can we co-produce with them? There was a very strong desire from all our producers.”
	

	“The goal isn’t for Reese to produce more herself, because she’s already produced a lot, but for this to also to fuel and create co-productions with our various producers. That’s what we’re hoping for,” he added.

	Asked about the skepticism surrounding the Hello Sunshine deal, similar to the doubts raised when Mediawan acquired Plan B, Capton pointed to the latter’s recent hits. 

	“Plan B has produced ‘F1’ and ‘Adolescence’ last year. They’ve announced a pretty incredible lineup of series and films, so we’re very happy,” Capton said. “We had to trust each other, and it also took time to show what Mediawan was all about.”

	Capton also sees further avenues for Mediawan to expand its footprint in the U.S. “We’re going to continue. Peter Chernin’s arrival at the group has helped us become more ambitious, and with KKR’s support and the help of our local teams, we’re going to do something quite unique.” 

	While he declined to address rumors that Mediawan was one of the companies circling Lionsgate, he said, “In our model, the more we can distribute worldwide, the better off we’ll be. So, we’re looking at all possible opportunities.” 

	The French executive, who shares his time between Los Angeles and Paris, is also optimistic about the prospects for groups like Mediawan following the recent Paramount-Warner Bros. merger even as Skydance prepares to make massive cuts.  

	“Skydance has committed to producing a certain number of films each year. I believe we have a company built on the creativity of our talent, and so, together, we’ll continue to develop and produce even more,” he said, citing “Backrooms” (North Road), “Adolescence” (Plan B) and Florian Zeller’s “Bunker” (Blue Morning Pictures), starring Javier Bardem and Penelope Cruz, were made by producers who are part of Mediawan. “I’m convinced that these successes will only grow with our global consolidation,” he continued, before revealing that the company will soon announce a major deal on vertical formats.

schema.headline: Mediawan’s Pierre-Antoine Capton on Buying Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine and Doubling Down on Hollywood Amid Consolidation (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Whalefall’ Review: Austin Abrams Gets Swallowed by a Whale in an Unintentionally Preposterous Thriller — a Tale of Human Perseverance and Mammalian Stomach Lining
description: “Whalefall” is an undersea thriller that would like to do for whales what “Jaws” did for sharks. But it doesn’t work out that way. The movie comes
body:
“Whalefall” is an undersea thriller that would like to do for whales what “Jaws” did for sharks. But it doesn’t work out that way. The movie comes closer to doing for whales what “Howard the Duck” did for barnyard superheroes — it makes you never want to see one of them again. Whales, of course, are beautiful creatures, and the one in “Whalefall” is a sperm whale with the boxy shape of a submarine, long and angular, a sleekly gliding beast that rules the ocean. Yet for most of the movie, we’re inside that whale. Literally inside it. The central character, Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams), has gone scuba diving off the coast of Monastery Beach near Monterey, Ca., in search of the body of his father, a gruff seaman who committed suicide. (He had mesothelioma, a form of cancer that meant he couldn’t dive anymore; for him, that meant life was no longer worth living.)
	

	After submerging himself, Jay gets entangled in the tentacles of a giant squid, and that’s when the whale, who feeds on squid, pulls both Jay and the squid into his oversize gaping mouth. Moments later, Jay is trapped inside, surrounded by gooey protrusions of undulating flesh. For the rest of the movie, he’ll attempt to survive inside that whale, which means keeping himself from getting sucked out of the creature’s digestive antechamber (which glows phosphorescent blue) and into its inner stomach cavity (which glows a hellish red), where the stomach acid will start to dissolve him.


	For a moment, it occurred to me that Jay might run into his father, à la Jonah or Geppetto. But no, he’s on his own, doing all he can to escape this tight squeeze of whale flesh. Is it gross? At times. Claustrophobic? A bit. Scary? Not even a little. The place Jay finds himself looks like a colonoscopy designed by H.R. Giger. The visual effects are…okay. At times, it’s as if we were locked in some pop-up theme-park ride called Full Cavity Search. At one point, Jay uses a jellyfish the whale has eaten to light his way, and that’s as close as he comes to finding a companion. “Whalefall” is a fearless tale of human perseverance and mammalian stomach lining. It should have been called “Project Hail Fish Guts.”
	

	Watching “Whalefall,” I kept thinking, “Why would anyone want to see this movie?” But the answer is obvious. “Whalefall” was adapted from Daniel Kraus’s 2023 novel, which in addition to being a bestseller was greeted with a great deal of acclaim. But something got lost in the translation. The thuddingly literal-minded movie that director Brian Duffield has made of it is a piece of thriller kitsch, full of unintentional laughs. With a hero who spends the heart of the film sucking on his oxygen mouthpiece, not so much talking as making frantic grunts of fear, “Whalefall” shuts us off from the most basic rooting interest. Sure, we want to see Jay get the hell out of there, but only because the whole ordeal is so stultifying and unpleasant.

	It’s saying something that this is the second movie in a month where Austin Abrams has to fight his way out of the grip of fleshy tentacles, and only one of those movies isn’t terminally preposterous, and that’s “Resident Evil.” Abrams had an indie-hipster-on-the-run appeal in Zach Cregger’s horror hit, but in “Whalefall” he’s too wimpy by half, a simpering college kid who never proves to the audience that he has the right stuff. The film, like the book, takes off from the troubled relationship between Jay and his father, Mitt, played by Josh Brolin with a mean glare and body tattoos, in one of those brusquely overstated performances as an abusive macho dad — a Not So Great Santini who thinks the best way to prepare his son for what a tough world it is out there is to make the kid hate and respect him, in that order. As Brolin plays him, Mitt is like Robert Shaw’s Quint in “Jaws,” only ratcheted up several notches of boozy psycho masochism.

	The film keeps jumping to flashbacks of Jay and Mitt at different points in their relationship, which is basically one long downhill slide. By the second half, though, Jay starts to realize that Mitt has actually taught him everything he needs to know to free himself from his predicament. The message? The young man who bonds with the ghost of his a–hole father while trapped in a gooey cushion of whale intestines stays with the ghost of his a–hole father. “Whalefall” even has an “ecological” side: The title refers to what happens when a whale’s carcass sinks to the ocean floor, an event that can give rise to a rich marine ecosystem. But “Whalefall,” the movie, is a carcass of a thriller that never rises.

schema.headline: ‘Whalefall’ Review: Austin Abrams Gets Swallowed by a Whale in an Unintentionally Preposterous Thriller — a Tale of Human Perseverance and Mammalian Stomach Lining

title: ‘Hazara Town,’ About the Hazara Community in Pakistan, Acquired by Filmotor Ahead of IDFA World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
description: World sales outfit Filmotor has acquired the global sales rights to “Hazara Town,” the debut feature documentary by Khadim Dai. The film will have
body:
World sales outfit Filmotor has acquired the global sales rights to “Hazara Town,” the debut feature documentary by Khadim Dai. The film will have its world premiere in the International Competition at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam, known as IDFA.

	Filmed over six years, “Hazara Town” is a “chronicle of survival, exile and the bond of family,” Filmotor said. Forced from Central Afghanistan by the Taliban in 1998, Dai’s family sought refuge in a walled enclave in Quetta, Pakistan, where the Hazara community continues to face targeted violence. Following a 2013 school bombing that killed 126 people—including Dai’s classmates—his family urged him to flee.
	

	After four failed attempts to reach Australia by boat and years spent stranded in Indonesia, Dai returned to Quetta in 2019 to film his community before their stories faded.


	The documentary captures the family’s daily life alongside their gradual, painful dispersal across the globe: his parents relocating to Canada, Dai and his niece taking refuge in the United States, and remaining relatives settling in Australia.

	“Restrictions on filming kept my camera largely within the home, school and cemetery. I wanted to bear witness to the slow disappearance of my community,” Dai said. “Years from now, someone might find this film and come to know them. I cannot bring my classmates back or restore the years of family separation, but I can pass on something of their lives through cinema. That possibility kept me filming.”

	The producing team said in a statement, “It is Khadim’s first feature film, but also the first film of its kind made in Quetta, a city in Pakistan far removed from the world’s gaze. We believe the film offers a rare opportunity to encounter the lives, experiences and perspectives of the Hazara people, who remain largely absent from cinema.”
	

	“Having tracked ‘Hazara Town’ since its pitch at Sunny Side of the Doc in 2023, we knew immediately that this was a story the world needed to see,” said Petar Mitric from Filmotor. “Khadim Dai’s deeply personal lens captures raw, human emotion in a way that is both heartbreaking and essential.”

	“Hazara Town” is produced by Ilyas Yourish for Congoo (Belgium), and co-produced by Khadim Dai, Graeme Isaac for Mayfan Films (Australia), and Anke Petersen and Lilian Tietjen for Jyoti Film (Germany).

	The film will compete for the IDFA Best Film and IDFA Best First Film Award.

	The project was developed with support from the Sundance Institute Documentary Film Program (with Open Society Foundations), the IDFA Bertha Fund Classic, Asian Cinema Fund, DMZ Industry (Special Jury Award), Docs Up Fund, Close Up Initiative, InMaat Foundation, Flanders Audiovisual Fund (VAF), MOIN Filmförderung Hamburg and Documentary Australia, among others.

schema.headline: ‘Hazara Town,’ About the Hazara Community in Pakistan, Acquired by Filmotor Ahead of IDFA World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Nia Long Joins Teyana Taylor’s Directorial Debut ‘Get Lite’ at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
After starring in the blockbuster biopic “Michael,” Nia Long has joined the cast of Teyana Taylor‘s directorial debut “Get Lite.”

	The Paramount m
body:
After starring in the blockbuster biopic “Michael,” Nia Long has joined the cast of Teyana Taylor‘s directorial debut “Get Lite.”

	The Paramount movie stars Emmy winner Storm Reid and NFL rookie-turned-actor Ceyair Wright. Wright (“Space Jam: A New Legacy”) plays a talented, but sheltered, dance student who finds inspiration, love and family in the last place he expected: the subways of New York City. Reid (“The Last of Us,” “Euphoria”) is the girl who opens his life to new possibilities.
	

	The role reunites Long and Reid after they co-starred in the hit 2023 thriller “Missing”; Long has also appeared in multiple projects for producer Kenya Barris, including his 2023 Netflix comedy “You People” and his 2020 series “#BlackAF.” She joins an acclaimed ensemble cast that features Leslie Odom, Jr., Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor, Jodie Turner-Smith, Asante Blackk, Woody McClain, Tylil James and Khayr Bullock.


	Production on “Get Lite” is underway in New York City, with Taylor directing from a screenplay by Maurice Williams, based on a spec script by Eric Gross that appeared on the Black List in 2020. Paramount has slated the film for a wide theatrical release on Aug. 20, 2027.

	In addition to starring in the film, Reid will produce alongside Barris and Anni Weisband for Khalabo Ink Society; Robyn Simpson for A Seed & Wings Productions, Reid’s banner; and Bill Karesh for Offbrnd. Taylor is also producing the film with Courtney “Coco” Gilbert, under their production banner, The Aunties.

	Last month, Long, a four-time NAACP Image Award winner, received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, literally cementing her status as a film and TV icon. She most recently starred in “Michael,” the blockbuster biopic about late pop star Michael Jackson, directed by Antoine Fuqua and produced by Oscar winner Graham King. The Lionsgate film grossed more than $1 billion worldwide, surpassing “Oppenheimer” as the highest-grossing biopic of all time. In the film, Long portrays Katherine Jackson, matriarch of the Jackson family, alongside Oscar nominee Colman Domingo as Joe Jackson and Jaafar Jackson, Michael Jackson’s nephew, as the king of pop.
	

	Up next, Long executive produces and stars in the Netflix film “Don’t Ever Wonder,” reuniting with her “Love Jones” co-star Lorenz Tate. She is also set to star with Ice Cube in “Are We Done Yet?“, the third film in their “Are We There Yet?” family comedy franchise, and reprise her role in the next “Friday movie.” 

	Long’s memoir — which chronicles her life and career, including iconic roles in “Boyz n the Hood,” “The Best Man” franchise, “Soul Food,” “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” “Third Watch,” “Tyler Perry’s The Single Mom’s Club,” “Dear White People,” “Fatal Affair,” The Banker,” “Roxanne, Roxanne” and more — will be published in 2027. 

	Long is represented by Untitled Entertainment and Brecheen Feldman Breimer Silver & Thompson, LLP.

schema.headline: Nia Long Joins Teyana Taylor’s Directorial Debut ‘Get Lite’ at Paramount (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ESPN Launches ESPN JV YouTube Channel for Kids
description:
ESPN JV isn’t for second-stringers.

	The new YouTube channel aims to cultivate younger sports fans who will keep the Disney sports-media giant in
body:
ESPN JV isn’t for second-stringers.

	The new YouTube channel aims to cultivate younger sports fans who will keep the Disney sports-media giant in mind as they grow up. The new channel, to be found at youtube.com/@ESPNJV will feature interactive challenges and appearances by both familiar Disney characters and top sports figures as well as videos that test viewers’ sports knowledge and explore memorable sports moments.


	“ESPN JV is about creating an exciting entry point into sports for the next generation of fans,” said Celia Bouza, ESPN’s vice president of multi-platform video, in a statement. ” By combining ESPN’s connection to the biggest moments and personalities in sports with creative, interactive storytelling, we’re building a destination where kids can explore their interests, discover new sports and develop a lifelong love of the game.”
	

	The launch of the new outlet marks ESPN’s latest attempt to bring young kids and their families to its screen. Over the past several years, the Disney sports division has tapped Marvel super heroes, “Toy Story” and “Inside Out” figures and characters from the popular cartoon “Big City Greens” for sundry alternative telecasts of basketball and hockey games, among other events.

	The channel will feature an original animated series, “The Sports Explorers,” which stars an “ESPN Squad.”  Ez, Shay, PJ and Nora each bring unique perspectives to the world of sports, helping young fans discover new games. The series was developed through a creative collaboration between ESPN and WSC Studios, the creative production arm of WSC Sports.
	

	ESPN says new videos will be added regularly.

	.

schema.headline: ESPN Launches ESPN JV YouTube Channel for Kids

title: From Bob Hope to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to ‘Wicked: One Wonderful Night’: How NBC Became America’s Home for TV Specials
description: It didn’t get great reviews. The host was awkward on camera as he navigated the emerging medium. The musical numbers and sketches didn’t translate
body:
It didn’t get great reviews. The host was awkward on camera as he navigated the emerging medium. The musical numbers and sketches didn’t translate well to the home screen.

	But none of it mattered. Bob Hope’s first-ever television special for NBC — “The Frigidaire Star Spangled Revue” — was a big hit with viewers when it aired in the late afternoon in Eastern time zones on Easter Sunday, April 9, 1950.


	Hope was already a big box office draw and a major radio star for NBC. He was the first of the big radio comedy titans to try out a TV program. He earned a whopping $40,000 (from Frigidaire) for the first special. A few months later, Variety reported that Hope had signed with Frigidaire for six more NBC specials, also for $40,000 apiece (or about $555,000 today).
	

	Hope would go on to host another 283 variety and comedy specials for NBC over the ensuing 46 years. The run, which included specials broadcast from behind the lines during the Vietnam War, remains a hallmark of longevity between a star and a network. It helped cement NBC’s reputation as a home for big entertainment specials and live events.

Bob Hope (1903-2003) honed his comedy chops in the waning years of vaudeville, grinding his way through short sets and long bills in the late 1920s and ‘30s. That experience set him up for a nearly 60-year run of hosting TV variety specials for NBC. #NBC100@nbc @UniversalTV pic.twitter.com/EmStRt0xh6— Variety (@Variety) October 12, 2026


	In radio and TV, NBC has consistently invested in special events to offset its regularly scheduled series. Some were designed to draw huge crowds to one-night-only performances, such as the famed 1983 concert special “Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever.” Some were designed to become annual traditions, such as the Tournament of Roses parade, the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree Lighting and the reigning champion of NBC’s holiday specials, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.
	

	“Today’s special is money in the bank for both the sponsor and the network,” Variety reported in 1957, when we also noted that ABC and CBS had gone “spec-happy,” following NBC’s lead.

	For NBC, the company born as a radio network that is marking its 100th anniversary this year, the specials tradition endures. NBC delivered a surprise smash 13 years ago with an ambitious live musical staging of “The Sound of Music” starring Carrie Underwood. More recently, NBC brought Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande together for the musical special late last year, “Wicked: One Wonderful Night” that doubled as promotion for Universal Pictures’ theatrical release of “Wicked: For Good.”



	

					Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande perform on 2025’s “Wicked: One Wonderful Night” special
									Griffin Nagel/NBC
	




	Many of NBC’s top franchises are decades-old traditions that have become part of the annual calendar for viewers, a way to mark time between seasons. That’s a gift from NBC’s stewards of the past to the current generation of executives. Jen Neal, executive VP of live events and specials for NBC and Peacock, never takes it for granted. 

	“The audience’s desire for these communal experiences are as vital as ever — even more so today than in past years because there’s so much going on in the world,” Neal tells Variety. “At a time when media is very fragmented and there are so many options and so many places that you can consume content, live TV still remains one of the most powerful ways to bring people together.”

	For advertisers as well as viewers, there’s something extra special about reaching viewers at a time when they’re likely to be reflective and nostalgic, especially around the holiday season. 

	“Live TV events does this differently than anything else,” Neal says. “NBCUniversal does that extraordinarily across sports and Olympics and news. But with the big live specials, it’s truly the place that you can bring people together for those habitual patterns during certain times of year.”

	Here’s a look at some of the event-izing of its airwaves in roughly its first 50 years.

	1938Bob Hope is tapped to host NBC’s “The Pepsodent Show,” which vaults him to radio stardom and begins Hope’s 60-year partnership with NBC.
	



	

					Bob Hope
									Getty Images
	



	1951NBC televises the annual Christmas tree lighting in Rockefeller Center for the first time as part of “The Kate Smith Show.”

	1953The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade airs on NBC as an hourlong special. In 1969, the parade telecast expanded to three hours. Today, the broadcast draws more than 20 million viewers. This year marks the 100th anniversary of the parade.



	

					The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in 1999
									Craig Blankenhorn/NBCU Photo Ban
	



	1954NBC owner RCA introduces its cutting-edge color television system with the New Year’s Day broadcast of the Tournament of Roses parade.

	1964NBC first airs the Golden Globes. By the 2000s, the show was enshrined as an important precursor to the Oscars. Ricky Gervais as well as Tina Fey and Amy Poehler are among the NBC-affiliated stars who made multiple appearances as hosts of the kudocast during the NBCUniversal era.



	

					Tina Fey and Amy Poehler host the Golden Globe Awards in 2013
									Paul Drinkwater/NBC
	



	1968“Elvis, the ’68 Comeback Special” marks Elvis Presley’s return to live performances. It is renowned as one of the most-watched concert specials of all time.



	

					Elvis Presley from his 1968 comeback special
									NBCU Photo Bank
	



	1974“The Dean Martin Celebrity Roast” series of specials begins a 10-year stretch of bawdy ribbing and playful skewering. Guests included everyone from then-California Gov. Ronald Reagan to Truman Capote to Joe Namath.



	

					Dean Martin, Don Rickles and Orson Welles on an early installment of “The Dean Martin Celebrity Roast.”
									Paul W. Baley/NBC
	



	1976NBC airs the 4½-hour special “NBC: The First 50 Years.”

	(Pictured top: Bob Hope and George Burns)

schema.headline: From Bob Hope to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to ‘Wicked: One Wonderful Night’: How NBC Became America’s Home for TV Specials

title: RadicalMedia’s New CEO Wants to Test Business Models That Give Production Powerhouse Stakes in Work It Does for Others
description:
At production powerhouse RadicalMedia, the only thing constant is change.

	Originally conceived as a way for founders Jon Kamen and Frank Scherma
body:
At production powerhouse RadicalMedia, the only thing constant is change.

	Originally conceived as a way for founders Jon Kamen and Frank Scherma to explore new content formats after many years in the advertising business, the firm now has a reputation as a go-to place for music documentaries, branded entertainment and long-form content. Radical Media has touched everything from the Questlove musical documentary “Summer of Soul” to the streaming version of “Hamilton” that made its way to Disney+ to “This Is a Gardening Show,” the offbeat Zach Galifinakis series on Netflix that is built from episodes just 15 minutes long.
	

	The founders intend to keep testing new frontiers, with one tweak to the company’s leadership ranks. Justin Barocas, a founder of the Anomaly agency, is taking up the reins as CEO, while Kamen will move to an executive-chairman role and Scherma will maintain his position as president. With that move, Barocas would like to see the company increase the number of theatrical properties it takes from Broadway to screens, and move into taking a greater amount of ownership in the content it creates.


	“It’s not very different from what we see in the marketplace now where the work-for-hire and the services business is changing,” says Barocas, during a recent interview at Radical’s offices in downtown Manhattan. “Being able to commercialize it in very different ways is one of the key areas.” RadicalMedia could look at models that include co-financing, maintaining backend rights, developing proprietary formats, and retaining underlying rights in stage adaptations and branded projects.
	

	Across the advertising ecosystem, owning some of the work created for ads and other promotions has long been a sort of Holy Grail. Many ad concepts become pieces of popular culture, spurring everything from memes to merchandise. Agencies, which once relied on a steady commission, never really got to benefit from any ancillary uses of the intellectual properties they had a hand in creating.

	Many have tried. In 2006, for example, the agency once known as Crispin Porter + Bogusky, took a minority stake in the Haggar clothing company as part of its arrangement with the manufacturer. But similar work continues today. Many media agencies are developing practices in what is called “principal media,” a term meant to describe the process of buying up commercial inventory from media companies and re-selling it to advertisers, rather than simply negotiating prices and placements.

	RadicalMedia is testing these waters as more advertisers demonstrate a yen to create their own content. Geico is working on a holiday-themed special that is expected to utilize the many ad characters it has created over the years. Athletic-clothing brand Under Armour has set up its own internal studio to better handle its content needs as more advertisers work to capture consumer attention across a wider array of media outlets.

	“The idea of being able to use entertainment to solve brand challenges and really commercialize our strengths is where I think what we’re working on in terms of the future. This is the destination for music storytelling, whether it’s theater adapting to streaming or television, whether it’s artists who want to tell their story in a different way,” says Barocas who says that “being able to take that strength and commercialize it” will give Radical Media an incentive “to be true partners” with advertisers, artists and media and entertainment companies.

	Kamen sees the new moves as part of the original maneuvers that originally gave rise to Radical. The “constant disruption” of the media and marketing industries “has been going on forever,”: he says. When he and Scherma founded the company, “we always looked and wanted for Radical to have an attitude of embracing whatever those changes will be. HE adds: “We’ve sometimes been ahead of the curve.”
	

	In an earlier era, Radical Media was involved with an MTV dating series, “Gamekillers,” that was produced along with the advertising agency BBH and was backed by a sponsorship from Unilever’s Axe deodorant. Some of the personality types used in the show were also featured in Axe commercials. And Radical enjoyed a long working relationship with the iconoclastic ad agency Wieden + Kennedy, which devised work for Nike that took the company well beyond the typical 30 second commercial.

	New concepts with similar themes have surfaced in the broadband era. Some advertisers can back documentaries or series that end up alongside more traditional content selections on Amazon’s Prime Video or NBCUniversal’s Peacock. “There’s no question that brand dollars are going to continue to play a role, even in this streaming universe,” says Kamen. Marketers will need to determine how to make advertising part of the on-demand experience, but “How do you do that effectively? How do you do that tastefully? How do you do that while embracing an audience and making sure that you’re appreciated for having brought something?”

	The executives say Radical’s current team will remain in place. Chris Kim, Dave Sirulnick and Jim Bouvet, who head up the company’s studio, entertainment and commercials divisions, respectively are expected to continue in their roles.

	Barocas is in many ways making a return to RadicalMedia, rather than an arrival. He worked alongside Radical’s team when he held a job at Wieden, and Kamen gave Barocas and others time to develop Anomaly in Radical’s offices. He intends to keep burnishing the company’s hard won skills in bringing advertisers “something incredibly different” than others, Barocas says. In an industry that is shifting to accommodate new technology, even RadicalMedia wants one thing to remain the same — its reputation.

schema.headline: RadicalMedia’s New CEO Wants to Test Business Models That Give Production Powerhouse Stakes in Work It Does for Others

title: ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Trailer: The Wilderness Survivors Return Home
description:
“Yellowjackets” is back — and the survivors have made it out of the wilderness.

	Paramount+ has released the teaser trailer for “Yellowjackets” Se
body:
“Yellowjackets” is back — and the survivors have made it out of the wilderness.

	Paramount+ has released the teaser trailer for “Yellowjackets” Season 4. The psychological horror returns to the streamer for the final time on Nov. 20.

	So far, “Yellowjackets” has chronicled the saga of an all-girls high school soccer team that becomes stranded in the woods after their plane crashes, and “their descent from a complicated but thriving team to savage clans, while also tracking the lives they’ve attempted to piece back together nearly 25 years later, proving that the past is never really past and what began out in the wilderness is far from over.”
	

	Now, after 19 months and a number of brutal deaths, the girls have been rescued and are adjusting to life back in New Jersey.  “As the survivors race to bury their sins before rescue arrives and an old flame roars back into town with plans of her own, turns out not every homecoming is a joyous one, and this one’s going to sting,” reads the fourth season’s official description. 


	Melanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, Tawny Cypress, Sophie Nélisse, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Sophie Thatcher, Samantha Hanratty, Courtney Eaton, Liv Hewson, Warren Kole, Kevin Alves, Sarah Desjardins, Nia Sondaya, Jenna Burgess and Hilary Swank are all back for Season 4. Guest starring are June Squibb, Elijah Wood, Molly Ringwald, Devon Sawa, Sam Braun, Dulé Hill and more.

	“Yellowjackets” is executive produced by showrunners and co-creators Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson. Drew Comins of Creative Engine also serves as executive producer along with Jonathan Lisco, Jeff W. Byrd, Sarah L. Thompson, Ameni Rozsa and Julia Bicknell. The series is produced for Showtime by Lionsgate Television.
	

	All previous seasons of “Yellowjackets” are available to watch now with the Premium plan on Paramount+

title: Jamie Foxx Boards Indie Crime Thriller ‘East of the River’ as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Jamie Foxx has joined the indie crime thriller “East of the River” as a producer. He boards through his Foxxhole Productions alongside Alex Marks.
body:
Jamie Foxx has joined the indie crime thriller “East of the River” as a producer. He boards through his Foxxhole Productions alongside Alex Marks.

	The film, directed by Dennis Latos, follows two estranged brothers reuniting to face the underground poker ring that destroyed their family. The film stars Ben Barnes (“The Chronicles of Narnia” franchise, “The Punisher”), Ben Ahlers (“The Gilded Age,” “Little Brother”), Callie Hernandez (“The Flight Attendant,” “Alien: Covenant”) and Maria Sten in here first film role since starring in television’s “Neagley.”
	

	The cast also includes David Zayas (“Dexter,” “Dexter: Resurrection”), John Bedford Lloyd (“Ozark”, “The Bourne Supremacy”), Catherine Curtin (“Stranger Things,” “Orange Is the New Black”), Nathan Wallace (“Daredevil: Born Again,” “NCIS: Origins”), and Steven Gregory (“Gravesend”). The film also features former WWE wrestler James Storm and former NFL running back Dalvin Cook.


	Post-production of the film recently wrapped. Global distribution rights are available through CAA Media Finance.

	“East of the River” was and written by Elise Finnerty with story by Jim Tamburino. Ben Grant served as director of photography on the film.

	In addition to Foxx and Marks, the film is produced by Nicolas Alvo at Ruta 5 Films, and Benjamin Wiessner at Vanishing Angle, alongside Latos and Finnerty. Executive producers include David Schuster of Gloves Up Entertainment Steven Gregory, John Harms, Gerry Ambrose and Foxx’s daughter Corinne Foxx. The film is presented by Gloves Up Entertainment in association with Echo Bend Productions.
	

	“We’ve been fans of Dennis since first discovering his short film, ‘Leylak’, where his command of character and storytelling immediately stood out. This film is a powerful continuation of that voice, and we’re proud to support this exceptional project,” Jamie and Corrine Foxx and Marks said in a joint statement.

	Latos said, “I wanted to capture the kinetic, dangerous energy of a world most people never see. This isn’t just a story about poker, it’s a high-octane look at what happens when you’re backed into a corner and forced to gamble with your life. We’ve fused a gritty family drama with the pulse-pounding stakes of the criminal underworld to give the audience a cinematic experience that is both deeply felt and truly thrilling.”

	Schuster added, “When Dennis Latos and I set out to make our first independent feature film, I never imagined that we’d have such a talented cast and amazing crew. With Dennis and I originally being from Queens, this project is close to our hearts. I am grateful to our amazing producing partners, Jamie, Alex, Nicolas, Benjamin, and Elise.”

	Barnes is represented by Gersh, Luber Roklin Entertainment and ID Public Relations. Ahlers is represented by Gersh, Artists First and Felker Toczek Suddleson McGinnis Ryan LLP. Hernandez is represented by Independent Artist Group, Entertainment 360 and Paul Hastings. Sten is represented by CAA, Brillstein Entertainment Partners, The Initiative Group and Granderson Des Rochers. Zayas is represented by Buchwald, ATA Management, Jill Fritzo Public Relations and Schreck Rose Dapello Adams Berlin & Dunham. Bedford Lloyd is represented by CESD Talent Agency. Curtin is represented by Artists & Representatives, Fusion Entertainment and Sullivan Talent Group. Wallace is represented by UIA Talent & Brian Twohig of Roger Paul Talent. Gregory is represented by Bright Artists Management.

title: Skydance Shares Skid Down 25% After Company Issues 471 Million Stock Warrants to Paramount Investors
description: Shares of Skydance Corp., formed through the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, fell as much as 25% in trading Wednesday. The drop cam
body:
Shares of Skydance Corp., formed through the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, fell as much as 25% in trading Wednesday. The drop came as the Skydance, led by chairman and CEO David Ellison, distributed about 471 million warrants giving holders of Paramount Skydance’s PSKY Class B shares the option to purchase stock in the new company. 

	As of 11 a.m. ET, the stock price of Skydance — which began trading Oct. 6 on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “SKYD” — was down 25.4%, to $6.78/share. The company’s current market capitalization is estimated at about $34.5 billion.
	

	Each warrant issued to PSKY holders initially allows them to buy one share of Skydance for $12. If all of those warrants were exercised, that would raise about $5.65 billion for the company, while it would also increase the share count and dilute ownership of current shareholders. It’s not known how many warrants have been exercised so far.


	In connection with Skydance’s distribution of stock warrants to PSKY holders, the NYSE announced after market close Tuesday that it will adjust the official closing price of Skydance’s Class B common stock downward by $0.19368 per share (from approximately $9.27 to approximately $9.07) based on the official closing price of the warrants of $2.20 (trading on NYSE under “SKYD WS”).

	The warrants issued to PSKY shareholders are intended to provide them the opportunity to purchase shares of Skydance’s Class B common stock “on similar terms” to those offered to the parties in the $47 billion equity syndicate backing the Warner Bros. Discovery deal, including David Ellison; his father, Larry Ellison; Gerry Cardinale, head of RedBird Capital Partners; LionTree; and the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Those equity investments in SKYD were priced at $12 per share.
	

	While the movement of Skydance’s stock price Wednesday has more to do with the issuing of the stock warrants, Wall Street has not been bullish on the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. The company will have pro-forma annual revenue of nearly $70 billion — but it also will have to deal with almost $80 billion in net debt.

	The distribution of the warrants “marks the final step in the WBD transaction closing process,” Wells Fargo analysts led by Steven Cahall said in a research note published Wednesday morning. They noted that “media mergers have a less than ideal history in terms delivering on pro-forma EBITDA expectations,” citing CBS and Viacom, Disney and 21st Century Fox and Discovery and WarnerMedia. 

	That said, the Wells Fargo analysts wrote, “We think SKYD will successfully deliver its ~$6bn in planned cost synergies. The main risk is whether the integration and disruption causes some leakage in core ops, and/or whether Media fundamentals change or are disrupted by tech. This history means investors may discount pro forma EBITDA to account for the leverage & risk.” The firm has an “underweight” rating on Skydance’s stock with a 12-month price target of $7.00/share.

	The Paramount-WBD deal, valued at $111 billion including the assumption of WBD debt, brings together two major studios, TV networks including CBS, CNN, Comedy Central, MTV and TBS, and streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max.

	Last week, after the deal closed, Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz (former chief of Mattel) announced their senior executive leadership team for the new Skydance.

Humanoid Robot

body:
Humanoid Robot
                          Grabs Teenage Girls Butt In Germany?!?
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 14, 2026
                            9:03 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A 4-foot-tall humanoid robot allegedly grabbed a 16-year-old girl's butt in Germany ... and cops are now trying to determine if a human was remotely operating the bot.
      
    
            The alleged incident went down in Cologne -- a city in the Western part of the country -- on Sunday, according to the North Rhine-Westphalia Police.
      
    
            In a press release, cops say the girl was with her friends outside a fast-food restaurant just before midnight on Sunday when the robot approached her from behind, touched her buttocks and "made thrusting motions against her."
      

            Cops say they believe the robot's 16-year-old owner and his 19-year-old friend filmed the alleged assault, streamed it live online and acted as commentators.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police say they found the robot and the teenage boys a few blocks away shortly after the alleged assault ... the robot was in the truck of a Volkswagen, and the 16-year-old had placed the bot inside.
      
    
            Cops confiscated the robot and two mobile phones belonging to the suspects ... police are "investigating on suspicion of sexual harassment."

title: Sheriff Deputy in Texas Fired For Posting Photos of Herself Posing with Inmates
description:
Texas Sheriff Deputy
                          Say Cheese ... Fired For Posing With Inmates
body:
Texas Sheriff Deputy
                          Say Cheese ... Fired For Posing With Inmates
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 14, 2026
                            7:11 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A sheriff's deputy in Texas is now on the unemployment line after getting axed for posting social media photos of herself posing with inmates in jail and flipping off the camera.
      
    
            Detention Deputy Karla Beltran was fired Monday by the Bexar County Sheriff's Office after the photos surfaced. She started working for the department in July and was canned under the sheriff's "probationary dismissal" policy.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            In one photo, Beltran is seen in front of a window raising her middle fingers at the camera ... with female inmates behind her separated by glass. Other photos show Beltran and the prisoners flashing other hand gestures.
      

            It's unclear why Beltran posed for the photos ... but it certainly wasn't a smart move, because she's now out of a job. Beltran had only been on the job for about 100 days. She started July 1.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Per the Bexar County Sheriff's Office, Detention Deputies serve a one-year probationary period, during which time they can be dismissed if they fail to meet required standards, as in Beltran's case.

title: Fitness Influencer Arrested After Allegedly Shooting Uber Eats Driver
description:
Fitness Influencer Arrested
                          Allegedly Shot, Pistol-Whipped Uber Eats Driver
body:
Fitness Influencer Arrested
                          Allegedly Shot, Pistol-Whipped Uber Eats Driver
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 14, 2026
                            8:44 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A fitness influencer in Miami has been arrested after he allegedly shot and pistol-whipped an Uber Eats driver who investigators say made a move on his girl.
      
    
            Khuslen Saruultuya -- a fitness enthusiast who goes by Khuslen Khan online and boasts close to 18K followers on Instagram -- appeared in court on Tuesday in Miami-Dade County after he was arrested on an attempted felony murder charge and unrelated drug charges.
      
    
            According to the arrest report reviewed by local Miami TV station WSVN ... an Uber Eats driver delivered food to an apartment complex early Monday morning, and investigators say he met a woman outside the main lobby.
      

            The driver and the woman briefly spoke, cops say ... and the driver left and later returned to the complex hoping to possibly get the woman's phone number.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Cops allege Saruultuya then approached the driver in a gray Corvette and pulled a gun on him. Officers claim he then ordered the driver to lie on the ground before firing a shot that grazed the alleged victim's butt. He also allegedly smacked the driver in the back of the head with a gun and threatened to kill him.
      
    
            Officers say the woman then attempted to intervene while Saruultuya allegedly chased the driver around the Corvette while pointing the gun at him.
      
    
            Eventually, cops claim the driver got away from Saruultuya and drove himself to a local hospital where he was treated for his injuries.
      
    
            After he was arrested, cops say they searched Saruultuya's residence ... and discovered suspected narcotics -- including what they believe is cocaine, MDMA, ketamine, marijuana, psilocybin mushrooms and hundreds of prescription pills. Cops also say they seized more than $11K in cash, which they believe is connected to drug sales.
      
    
            During Saruultuya's court hearing, the judge in the case read the drug possession charges ... reading out "Trafficking in cocaine, trafficking in ecstasy, possession with intent to sell Adderall."
      
    
            According to previous reports, Saruultuya was arrested on drug trafficking charges back in 2023.
      
    
            He reportedly has a court hearing set for Wednesday to determine if he will be granted bail.

description:
Six Flags Over Georgia
                          Reopening Friday after Guest's Gruesome Death
body:
Six Flags Over Georgia
                          Reopening Friday after Guest's Gruesome Death
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 14, 2026
                            7:19 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Six Flags Over Georgia is set to reopen Friday ... just days after a man fell to his death after being ejected from one of the theme park's popular roller coasters.
      
    
            The investigation is ongoing, but local news outlet WSB-TV reports the park will open its doors Friday... though it's unclear whether Goliath, the ride from which the man fell, will remain closed. It seems unlikely the park would reopen it.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            As we reported ... Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was killed after he fell from the Goliath roller coaster.
      
    
            Hassan -- who was a member of a roller coaster enthusiasts club -- struck several other riders before hitting the ground, investigators say.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Six Flags temporarily closed 9 similar roller coasters around the United States after the tragedy.
      
    
            Bolliger & Mabillard -- the company that manufactures Goliath and other roller coasters -- is actively investigating the incident.
      
    
            Footage that appears to show him falling from the coaster is making the rounds on social media, and his family is pleading with folks to stop sharing it.
